languageSetup.title: Choose a display language
languageSetup.label: Display language
languageSetup.hint: You can change it later in Settings.

connections.title: Connections
connections.emptyBody: Add a computer to connect to, and choose the proxy it goes through. Proxies are added on the Proxies page; choose Direct when none is needed.
connections.subtitle: Each connection has its own local entrance address; Remote Desktop reaches the computer through it and the proxy.
connections.setProxyFailed: Could not change the proxy of “{{name}}”
connections.deleteBody: “{{name}}” will be deleted, together with its saved password and the user name and certificate trust Remote Desktop remembers for it.

form.locked: This connection is in use. Disconnect it to change its settings.
form.name: Name
form.addressHint: Computer name or IP address. If the port is not 3389, write address:port, such as pc.example.com:3390.
form.addressChanged: After the computer changes, the password saved for the old address is deleted.
form.usernameHint: Fills in Remote Desktop's sign-in. DOMAIN\user and user@domain both work.
form.remember: Remember the password (in Windows Credential Manager)
form.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved password; type one to replace it.
form.passwordHint: Optional: you can enter it when connecting.
form.noRememberHint: Without remembering, you are asked before each connection; the password is used for that connection only and deleted when it ends.
form.savedByMstsc: Remote Desktop itself remembers a password for this connection (“Remember me” at sign-in).
form.savedByApp: A password is saved for this connection.
form.screensMultimon: All monitors (one remote screen per monitor)
form.displayHint: Clipboard, drives, sound and the other settings come from Remote Desktop's default settings (Default.rdp in Documents), the same for every connection.

import.title: Import from an .rdp file
import.read: The computer, user name and display settings were read from “{{file}}”; check them and save. Clipboard, drives and the file's other settings are not imported: every connection uses Remote Desktop's default settings.
import.gateway: This file connects through an RD Gateway ({{server}}). The imported connection goes to the computer through the proxy instead, without the gateway.
import.gatewayUnnamed: This file connects through an RD Gateway. The imported connection goes to the computer through the proxy instead, without the gateway.
import.existing: Connections to this computer already exist: {{names}}.

password.title: Connect to “{{name}}”
password.label: Password for {{user}}
password.hint: You can also leave it empty and let Remote Desktop ask for it.

test.title: Check the route to “{{name}}”
test.proxyWhat: Fetching the test URL ({{host}}) through the proxy
test.targetWhat: Asking the Remote Desktop service on the remote computer to answer
test.securityWaiting: Waiting for the remote computer to answer
test.securityUnknown: The remote computer did not answer, so this is unknown

verdict.testUrlFailed: The route works. The test URL could not be fetched through the proxy, perhaps because that site is blocked where the proxy server is; Remote Desktop is not affected.
verdict.direct: The remote computer cannot be reached: check the computer's address and port, that it is on and allows Remote Desktop, and the firewalls in between.
verdict.beyondProxy: The proxy itself works, but the remote computer cannot be reached through it: check the computer's address and port, that it is on and allows Remote Desktop, and that the proxy server can reach it.
verdict.proxy: The problem is most likely the proxy: it could not fetch the test URL either. Check the proxy's settings (server, port, user ID or password) and that the proxy server is running.
verdict.settings: The connection's settings need fixing; see above.

protocols.hybridEx: {{name}}: Network Level Authentication (NLA). You enter the password on this computer before the remote desktop shows.
protocols.hybrid: {{name}}: Network Level Authentication (NLA). You enter the password on this computer first.
protocols.ssl: {{name}}: TLS without Network Level Authentication; the sign-in screen shows on the remote computer.
protocols.rdp: {{name}}: Standard RDP Security, the old encryption without TLS. Consider requiring TLS or Network Level Authentication on the remote computer.

failures.sslNotAllowed: {{name}}: the remote computer accepts only Standard RDP Security, the old encryption. Remote Desktop may still connect.
failures.sslCertMissing: {{name}}: the remote computer has no certificate to use, which leaves only Standard RDP Security. Remote Desktop may still connect.
failures.inconsistentFlags: {{name}}: the remote computer found the request inconsistent.
failures.hybridRequired: {{name}}: the remote computer requires Network Level Authentication (NLA).
failures.sslWithUserAuthRequired: {{name}}: the remote computer requires TLS with user authentication.
failures.other: {{name}}: the remote computer refused the security protocols offered. Remote Desktop may still connect.

log.title: Session log: {{name}}
log.empty: This connection has not been used since the app started.

proxies.title: Proxies
proxies.emptyTitle: No proxies of your own yet
proxies.emptyBody: Paste a share link exported from v2rayN or similar (vmess://, vless://, trojan://, ss://, hysteria2://), or enter a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, such as the local port of v2rayN or Clash (often 127.0.0.1:10808 or 7890).
proxies.subtitle: Connections can share a proxy, so switching servers is done in one place.
proxies.directHint: No proxy: connect to the remote computer directly
proxies.latencyHint: Fetches the test URL from Settings through this proxy and measures the time.
proxies.deleteMoves: These connections use it and will connect directly, without a proxy: {{profiles}}.
proxies.deleteConnected: These connections are connected through this proxy. Disconnect them to delete it: {{profiles}}.

form.locked: These connections are connected through this proxy. Disconnect them to change it: {{profiles}}.
form.name: Name
form.unsupportedKind: This kind of proxy can't be edited here.
form.linkHint: Paste a link exported from v2rayN or similar to fill in the settings below.
form.linkHintEdit: A new link replaces the settings below; the name stays.
form.linkImported: The settings below come from the link. Check them, then save.
form.userIdHint: A UUID, or the custom ID of 1–30 characters set on the server.
form.encryptionHint: The client setting of VLESS Encryption; keep none unless the server uses it.
form.obfsPasswordHint: Leave empty unless the server uses obfuscation; at least 4 characters.
form.seedHint: Only if the server sets one; it encrypts the packets.
form.realitySniHint: The site the REALITY server borrows, such as www.microsoft.com.
form.pinnedCertsHint: For a self-signed certificate, enter its SHA-256 hash. Xray no longer skips certificate checks.
form.finalMaskHint: The link's fm parameter: disguise headers, mKCP obfuscation and Salamander. Can't be used together with mKCP's header type and seed. For mKCP to a current Xray server without obfuscation, enter {"udp":[]}.
form.verifyNames: Names to verify the certificate against
form.verifyNamesHint: Checked instead of the SNI; separate several with commas.
form.outboundHint: One complete outbound object with a protocol; its tag is ignored.
form.customServerHint: Optional, only shown in the list; connections go where the JSON says.
form.secretsLost: This proxy's password and settings can't be decrypted (they come from another computer or Windows user), so what you see below are defaults, not its settings. Paste the share link again, or enter all the settings again, before saving.

proxies.linkCopied: Share link copied. It contains the password; share it only with people you trust.
proxies.secretsLostHint: Its password and settings can't be decrypted (they come from another computer or Windows user). It isn't used until saved again.

settings.title: Settings
settings.closeBehavior: When the main window is closed
settings.closeToTray: Minimize to the tray and keep running
settings.closeHint: While a remote desktop is connected through a proxy, the window always minimizes to the tray so the connection isn't cut.
settings.localPortHint: Each connection listens on this port at its own 127.x.y.z address. Applies to connections started afterwards.
settings.checkFirst: Check the route before starting Remote Desktop
settings.checkFirstHint: Makes sure the remote computer answers through the proxy first, so a broken route is explained at once instead of Remote Desktop waiting.
settings.testUrlHint: Fetched through a proxy when you test it on the Proxies page.
settings.urlInvalid: Enter a URL starting with http:// or https://.
settings.logLevelHint: Host names, IP addresses and user names are masked before they are written to the log file. The log folder is under Data below.
settings.dataIntro: Everything the app keeps is in the folder it runs from, where you can look at it.

dataFiles.webview2: The window's cache; can be deleted while the app isn't running

settings.dataSecrets: Proxy passwords are encrypted with Windows in these files: only this Windows account on this PC can read them, so after copying the folder elsewhere they need to be entered again. Remote Desktop passwords are kept in Windows Credential Manager, where Remote Desktop Connection reads them, not in this folder.

diag.title: Diagnostics
diag.subtitle: Settings and versions on this computer that affect Remote Desktop connections. Only read, never changed.
diag.copied: Diagnostics copied; paste them into a bug report. Server names and folders are left out.
diag.editDefaultsOpened: Remote Desktop Connection is open. If its options are hidden, click Show Options; change the settings on its tabs, then click Save on the General tab to keep them.
diag.editDefaultsFailed: Could not open Remote Desktop Connection
diag.openLogsFailed: Could not open the log folder

mstsc.label: Remote Desktop Connection (mstsc)
mstsc.missing: mstsc.exe is missing. This edition of Windows may lack Remote Desktop Connection; the app cannot work without it.

webview2.label: WebView2 Runtime
webview2.missing: The WebView2 Runtime was not found.

defaultRdp.label: Default settings file (Default.rdp)
defaultRdp.found: Present. Clipboard, drives, sound and the other settings of every connection through this app come from it.
defaultRdp.missing: Not yet. Remote Desktop uses its built-in defaults; saving once in “Change Remote Desktop's default settings” creates it.

gateway.label: RD Gateway
gateway.maybe: When it cannot connect directly, Remote Desktop may switch to an RD Gateway, which cannot reach this app's tunnel.
gateway.maybePolicy: Group Policy enables an RD Gateway: when it cannot connect directly, Remote Desktop switches to the gateway, which cannot reach this app's tunnel.
gateway.used: Remote Desktop is set to always connect through an RD Gateway, so connections through this app are stopped. In “Change Remote Desktop's default settings”, go to Advanced → Settings and choose “Do not use an RD Gateway server”.

serverAuth.label: If server authentication fails
serverAuth.refuse: Do not connect. Through the tunnel the name on the certificate never matches the entrance address, so Remote Desktop refuses to connect unless you trusted the computer's certificate before. Consider “Warn me” on the Advanced tab of “Change Remote Desktop's default settings”.
serverAuth.warn: Warn me. The first time Remote Desktop reaches a computer through the tunnel, it warns about the certificate; tick “Don't ask me again for connections to this computer” to stop it.
serverAuth.connectPolicy: Always connect, even if authentication fails (Group Policy “Configure server authentication for client”).
serverAuth.refusePolicy: Do not connect if authentication fails (Group Policy “Configure server authentication for client”). Through the tunnel the name on the certificate never matches the entrance address, so Remote Desktop refuses to connect unless you trusted the computer's certificate before. Only an administrator can change this policy.
serverAuth.warnPolicy: Warn me if authentication fails (Group Policy “Configure server authentication for client”). The first time Remote Desktop reaches a computer through the tunnel, it warns about the certificate; tick “Don't ask me again for connections to this computer” to stop it.

alwaysPrompt.label: Always ask for credentials
alwaysPrompt.yes: Yes. Remote Desktop asks for the password every time and does not fill in saved ones. Untick “Always ask for credentials” on the General tab of “Change Remote Desktop's default settings”.

savedCredentials.label: Saved passwords through the tunnel
savedCredentials.allowedDefault: Allowed. No policy says otherwise, and computers outside a domain allow them by default.
savedCredentials.allowedPolicy: Allowed. The policy “Allow delegating saved credentials with NTLM-only server authentication” covers every Remote Desktop server.
savedCredentials.deniedDefault: Not allowed. Computers in a domain do not use saved passwords by default when the server is authenticated with NTLM only, and through the tunnel it can be authenticated with NTLM only (127.x.y.z has no Kerberos name). Remote Desktop then says your system administrator does not allow saved credentials, and you type the password. An administrator can add TERMSRV/* to Computer Configuration → Administrative Templates → System → Credentials Delegation → “Allow delegating saved credentials with NTLM-only server authentication”.
savedCredentials.deniedPolicy: Not allowed. The policy “Allow delegating saved credentials with NTLM-only server authentication” is disabled.
savedCredentials.deniedByDeny: Not allowed. The policy “Deny delegating saved credentials” covers every server.
savedCredentials.limited: The policy allows saved passwords for the servers below only; this app's entrance addresses (127.x.y.z) are hardly among them.
savedCredentials.unknown: Unknown: whether this computer is in a domain could not be told, and that decides the default.

credentialGuard.label: Credential Guard
credentialGuard.running: Running. Passwords Remote Desktop saves itself (“Remember me”) may not be used; those this app saves are not affected.

encryptionOracle.label: CredSSP Encryption Oracle Remediation
encryptionOracle.forceUpdated: Force Updated Clients. Does not connect to remote computers without the CredSSP update, and this computer's Remote Desktop service does not accept clients without it either.
encryptionOracle.mitigated: Mitigated. Does not connect to remote computers without the CredSSP update.
encryptionOracle.vulnerable: Vulnerable. Also connects to remote computers without the update, which is unsafe.

logs.label: Log folder
logs.local: On a disk of this PC.

common.dataLoadFailed: Could not load the connections and proxies: {{message}}

net.refused: The connection was refused. Check the address and port, and that the service is running.
net.unreachable: The network or the computer is unreachable.
net.reset: The other side reset the connection.
net.dns: The computer name couldn't be found.
net.addressInUse: Another program is already using this local address and port.
net.accessDenied: Windows won't let the app use this local port. Hyper-V or WSL may have reserved it; choose another local port in Settings.
net.addressNotAvailable: This address isn't available on this computer.

probe.noAnswer: The connection closed before the remote computer answered. Through a proxy, the proxy may not reach the remote computer, or its user ID or password may be wrong (VMess, VLESS and Trojan proxies don't say why).
probe.notRdp: Something answered, but not a Remote Desktop server. Check the port.
probe.truncated: The remote computer's answer was cut short.
probe.malformed: The remote computer's answer isn't valid Remote Desktop data.

tunnel.noAnswer: The connection closed before the remote computer answered. Through a proxy, the proxy may not reach the remote computer, or its user ID or password may be wrong (VMess, VLESS and Trojan proxies don't say why).

proxy.auth: The proxy rejected the user name or password.
proxy.unreachable: Couldn't connect to the proxy server. Check that it's running and that its address and port are right.
proxy.targetFailed: The proxy couldn't connect to the remote computer.
proxy.dropped: The proxy closed the connection before the remote computer answered. Usually the proxy, or the server behind it, can't reach the remote computer.
proxy.unsupported: This kind of proxy isn't supported yet.
proxy.inUse: These connections use this proxy too: {{profiles}}. Check the list and delete again.
proxy.connected: These connections are connected through this proxy: {{profiles}}. Disconnect them to change or delete it.
proxy.tls: The proxy server's certificate didn't pass: it may not be the pinned certificate, or may not match the server name; with REALITY, the public key may be wrong.
proxy.secretsLost: This proxy's password and settings can't be decrypted (they come from another computer or Windows user), so it can't be used for now. Edit it: paste the share link again, or enter everything again, and save.

session.ending: The previous session of this connection is still ending. Connect again once it has ended.
session.loopbackDirect: The remote computer is this computer itself. Without a proxy the tunnel would connect to itself.
session.running: This connection is in use. Disconnect it first.

rdp.noAddress: The .rdp file doesn't say which computer to connect to.
rdp.tooLarge: This file is too large to be an .rdp file.

store.notFound: It no longer exists. It may have been deleted.
store.builtIn: The direct connection is built in and can't be changed.

secret.unreadable: A saved password can't be decrypted by this Windows user.

credential.failed: Windows Credential Manager refused the change.

gateway.used: Remote Desktop is set to always connect through an RD Gateway ({{server}}), which can't reach this app's tunnel. Turn the RD Gateway off in Remote Desktop Connection: Show Options → Advanced → Settings.

profile.proxyMissing: This connection's proxy no longer exists. Choose another one.

link.invalid: This isn't a valid share link.
link.unsupported: This app doesn't support “{{what}}” from the link.
link.transportRemoved: Xray no longer has the “{{network}}” transport (HTTP/2, QUIC). Ask the server's provider to switch to XHTTP or another transport.
link.notShareable: A custom Xray outbound has no share link.

store.unreadable: {{file}} couldn't be read. It was renamed to .corrupt and left out.
store.newerSchema: {{file}} was saved by a newer version of the app and was left out.
store.secretLost: The password and proxy settings in {{file}} can't be decrypted; the file may come from another Windows user or computer. Edit the proxy: paste the share link again, or enter everything again, and save.
store.loopbackMoved: {{file}} got a new loopback address because its old one was missing or used by another connection.
store.readFailed: {{file}} couldn't be opened, perhaps because another program is using it. It was left out and is unchanged.

settings.recovered: The settings file couldn't be read, so the defaults are in use. The old file was kept as settings.json.corrupt.

log.unavailable: The log file couldn't be opened. The log is kept in memory only.

credential.saveFailed: The password for “{{profile}}” couldn't be saved in Windows Credential Manager.
credential.deleteFailed: The saved password for “{{profile}}” couldn't be deleted.

mstsc.forgetFailed: What Remote Desktop remembers about “{{profile}}” couldn't be removed.

session.upstreamOk: The remote computer answered through the route.
session.upstreamFailing: A connection couldn't reach the remote computer: {{error}}
session.nothingToClose: Remote Desktop had no session window to close (it was connecting, asking for a password, or showing a dialog of its own), so it is ended. If you had signed in, the session on the remote computer stays.
session.tunnelFailed: The tunnel entrance stopped accepting connections: {{error}}
session.unexpectedEvent: Ignored an unexpected event {{event}} during step “{{step}}”.
session.gatewayMaybe: If Remote Desktop can't connect directly, it may switch to an RD Gateway ({{server}}), which can't reach this app's tunnel.
session.defaultsUnknown: Could not read Remote Desktop's default settings (Default.rdp): {{error}}
session.hintFailed: Couldn't pre-fill the user name for Remote Desktop: {{error}}
session.serverAuthRefuse: Remote Desktop's default settings say “If server authentication fails: Do not connect”. Through the tunnel the name on the certificate never matches the entrance address, so Remote Desktop refuses to connect unless you trusted this computer's certificate before.
session.alwaysPrompt: Remote Desktop's default settings say “Always ask for credentials”, so the saved password is not filled in; you will be asked again.
session.serverAuthRefusePolicy: The Group Policy “Configure server authentication for client” says “Do not connect if authentication fails”. Through the tunnel the name on the certificate never matches the entrance address, so Remote Desktop refuses to connect unless you trusted this computer's certificate before.

quit.title: Quit RDP over Proxy?
quit.body_one: {{count}} remote desktop is connected through this app. Quitting disconnects it.
quit.body_other: {{count}} remote desktops are connected through this app. Quitting disconnects all of them.

fieldErrors.requiredForPassword: A user name is needed to save a password.

linkNotes.insecure: The link asks to skip certificate checks, which Xray no longer does. The certificate will be checked; if the server's is self-signed, enter its SHA-256 hash under Certificate fingerprint.
linkNotes.alterId: VMess alterId {{value}} was ignored: Xray speaks only VMess AEAD. A server that still requires the old authentication won't accept the connection.
linkNotes.ports: The link uses port hopping ({{ports}}); this app uses port {{port}} only.
